ai.literal: Not despising the power of the capable is, among all protections of those who protect, the head.
ai.translation: Not scorning the power of the capable is the chief of all safeguards for those who guard themselves.
ai.modern: செயல்களைச் செய்து முடிக்கும் ஆற்றல் உடையவர்களை அவமதிக்காமல் இருப்பது, தம்மைக் காத்துக்கொள்ள விரும்புபவர் செய்யும் காவல்கள் எல்லாவற்றிலும் சிறந்ததாகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet emphasizes the importance of respecting powerful and capable people. It states that not scorning their abilities is the most effective way for a person to protect themselves from harm. The word 'ஆற்றுவார்' refers to those who have the power to accomplish things, while 'போற்றுவார்' refers to those who wish to guard their own well-being. By placing this respect as the 'head' (தலை) of all protections, the text highlights that avoiding the enmity of the great is the ultimate safeguard.

ai.literal: The great without respecting if one behaves, by the great un-departing sorrow it will give.
ai.translation: If one conducts oneself without respecting the great, it will bring unceasing sorrow caused by those very great ones.
ai.modern: பெரியவர்களை மதிக்காமல் ஒருவன் நடந்துகொண்டால், அந்தப் பெரியவர்களால் அவனுக்கு ஒருபோதும் நீங்காத துன்பம் வந்து சேரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the danger of disrespecting people of great power or virtue. The phrase 'பேணாது ஒழுகின்' describes conducting oneself without showing due honor to such individuals. If one acts this way, it will result in 'பேரா இடும்பை', which means sorrow that does not depart or cease. The word 'பெரியாரால்' emphasizes that the great themselves, or the very act of offending them, will be the direct cause of this unending affliction.

ai.literal: Ruin if desired, without listening let one do, destroying if desired towards those who are capable, an offense.
ai.translation: If one desires their own ruin, let them ignore advice and commit an offense against those capable of destroying them at will.
ai.modern: தான் கெட்டுப்போக விரும்பினால், ஒருவன் அறிவுரைகளைக் கேட்காமல், நினைத்தவுடனே அழிக்க வல்லவர்களிடத்தில் பிழையைச் செய்யட்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the fatal consequences of offending powerful people. The phrase 'அடல் வேண்டின் ஆற்றுபவர்' refers to those who have the capability to destroy someone the moment they wish to do so. If a person truly wants to be ruined, the surest way is to ignore all good advice ('கேளாது') and commit an offense ('இழுக்கு') against such formidable individuals. The use of the optative 'செய்க' (let them do) acts as a strong, ironic warning against such foolish behavior.

ai.literal: Death (acc.) by hand is like calling, to the powerful the powerless harm doing.
ai.translation: For the powerless to do harm to the powerful is like beckoning Death with their own hands.
ai.modern: வலியற்றவர்கள் வலிமை மிக்கவர்களுக்குத் தீங்கு செய்வது, தங்கள் கைகளால் எமனை அழைப்பதற்குச் சமமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the folly of provoking those who are stronger than oneself. The word 'ஆற்றுவார்' refers to the powerful who can accomplish things, while 'ஆற்றாதார்' refers to those lacking such power. By doing harm ('இன்னா செயல்') to the mighty, the weak are essentially bringing destruction upon themselves. The poet uses the striking image of beckoning Death ('கூற்றத்தை') with one's own hand ('கையால் விளித்தற்றால்') to illustrate the suicidal nature of such an act.

ai.literal: Wherever having gone, anywhere existing ones they will not become, of fierce strength by a king those who are angered at.
ai.translation: Those who have incurred the wrath of a king of fierce power will not survive anywhere, no matter where they flee.
ai.modern: கடுமையான வலிமையுடைய அரசனால் கோபிக்கப்பட்டவர்கள் எங்கு தப்பிச் சென்றாலும் எங்கும் உயிர்வாழ மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against offending powerful rulers. The phrase 'வெம் துப்பின் வேந்து' refers to a king possessing fierce and formidable strength. 'செறப்பட்டவர்' denotes those who have become the target of such a king's anger. The couplet emphasizes that no matter where these offenders flee ('யாண்டுச் சென்று'), they will not find a safe haven to survive ('யாண்டும் உளர் ஆகார்'). The repetition of 'யாண்டு' underscores the absolute impossibility of escaping the reach of a truly powerful leader once offended.

ai.literal: By fire even if burnt survival there is; they will not survive great ones having wronged those who behave.
ai.translation: Even those burnt by a fire might find a way to survive, but those who live by wronging the great will not escape.
ai.modern: நெருப்பால் சுடப்பட்டாலும் ஒருவர் தப்பிப் பிழைத்துக்கொள்ள முடியும்; ஆனால் ஆற்றல் மிக்க பெரியவர்களுக்குத் தீங்கு செய்து வாழ்பவர்கள் தப்பவே மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the physical danger of fire with the existential danger of offending great people. Even if someone is caught in a fire and severely burnt, there is still a chance they might escape and survive ('உய்வு உண்டாம்'). However, those who conduct their lives by wronging powerful and great individuals have absolutely no chance of survival ('உய்யார்'). The repetition of the root 'உய்' (to survive or escape) emphasizes that the wrath of the great is far more inescapable and destructive than fire itself.

ai.literal: arrangement excellent life-and vast wealth-and what will-become, dignity excellent worthy-persons if-they-are-angry?
ai.translation: What is the use of an excellently arranged life and vast wealth, if worthy men of excellent dignity grow angry?
ai.modern: தகுதியால் சிறந்த பெரியவர்கள் சினங்கொண்டால், ஒருவனுடைய பலவகையிலும் சிறந்த வாழ்க்கையும் பெரும் செல்வமும் என்ன பயனைத் தரும்?
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against incurring the wrath of great and worthy people. It asks what good a perfectly arranged life and immense wealth can do if one angers those of excellent character. The word 'செறின்' means 'if they become angry', showing that the displeasure of the great can destroy even the most secure and prosperous life. The repetition of 'மாண்ட' (excellent) contrasts the material excellence of one's life with the moral excellence of the worthy people.

ai.literal: Hill-like those to decrease if considered, with family having stood-like those will perish from the earth.
ai.translation: If one slights those whose greatness is like a mountain, even those who seem firmly established will perish from the earth along with their entire family.
ai.modern: மலை போன்ற பெருமை உடையவர்களைச் சிறுமைப்படுத்தி அவமதித்தால், நிலைபெற்று நிற்பது போல் தோன்றுபவர்களும் தங்கள் குடும்பத்தோடு உலகிலிருந்து அழிந்து போவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The couplet warns against disrespecting people of immense, mountain-like greatness ('குன்று அன்னார்'). If someone looks down upon them or treats them lightly ('குன்ற மதிப்பின்'), the consequences are devastating. Even if the offenders seem deeply rooted and firmly established ('நின்று அன்னார்'), they will be completely wiped from the earth, taking their entire lineage ('குடியொடு') with them. The contrast between the unshakeable mountain and the offenders who only appear to stand firm highlights the destructive power of offending the truly great.

ai.literal: Exalted principles-those if enraged, in the middle having broken, even a king kingship will perish.
ai.translation: If those of exalted principles become enraged, even a king will break mid-way and lose his kingdom.
ai.modern: உயர்ந்த கொள்கைகளை உடைய பெரியவர்கள் சினந்தால், ஒரு அரசனும் தன் இடையில் முறிந்து தன் அரச பதவியை இழந்து அழிவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the devastating consequences of angering people of high principles. The phrase 'ஏந்திய கொள்கையார்' refers to those who hold elevated, unwavering ideals. 'சீறின்' means if they hiss or become enraged, comparing their righteous anger to a snake's strike. The consequence is described vividly as 'இடை முரிந்து' (breaking in the middle), meaning the offender's life or reign will be snapped abruptly before its natural end. Even a powerful king ('வேந்தனும்') will lose his very kingship ('வேந்து கெடும்') if he incurs their wrath.

ai.literal: Exceedingly established support possessors even if (they are), they will not survive, excellently endowed great-ones if they are angry.
ai.translation: Even if they possess overwhelmingly strong support, they will not survive if men of eminent greatness become angry.
ai.modern: அளவுகடந்த வலிமையான பாதுகாப்பை உடையவராக இருந்தாலும், சிறந்த பெருமைகளை உடைய பெரியவர்கள் சினங்கொண்டால் அவர்கள் தப்ப மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against incurring the wrath of truly great people. The phrase 'இறந்து அமைந்த சார்பு' refers to having overwhelmingly strong support or protection, such as wealth, armies, or fortifications. However, the poet asserts that even such immense power is useless ('உய்யார்') against the anger of those who possess eminent greatness ('சிறந்து அமைந்த சீரார்'). The word 'செறின்' means 'if they become angry' or 'if they decide to destroy', emphasizing that the moral and spiritual power of the great can easily overcome any material defense.
